why: The answer gives one correct reason that ties how often you compile to where errors show up: if you compile after every few lines, each error sits in the code you just wrote, so debugging stays local.

concepts.quote: If you compile after every few lines, each error is next to the code you just wrote, so it is easy to find.
concepts.why: It makes the point that small steps keep debugging local, because the newest change is the first suspect.

concepts.quote: compile after every few lines, each error is next to the code you just wrote
concepts.why: It explains that compiling often means each error is found close to its cause, but only for this scenario, not as a rule for new programs.
The answer says nothing about how to read or interpret the 37 messages.
It mentions errors in general but says nothing about what compile-time errors are or how javac reports them.
